data.one_liner: Provides named integer constants for ASCII and HTML character codes.
data.what_it_does: The package defines symbolic names for character codes, making code that works with integer character values more readable. It also offers a CLI tool to generate a custom set of constants for a project.
use_when: You need readable constants for ASCII or common HTML entities in Dart code.
You want to avoid hard‑coding integer literals for characters.
You prefer a small, dependency‑free helper for character code lookups.
You plan to generate a custom file and keep the package as a dev dependency.
avoid_when: You already have a code‑generation tool that produces constants.
You need runtime access to a large set of Unicode characters beyond ASCII and HTML entities.
You prefer to use string literals instead of integer codes.
strengths: Zero runtime dependency, pure Dart constants.
Supports both ASCII and HTML entities with clear naming conventions.
CLI generator lets you create a trimmed set of constants for production.
No build_runner or code‑gen setup required for basic use.
weaknesses: Limited to ASCII and HTML 4.01 entities; no full Unicode support.
Requires manual generation for custom sets if you want to drop unused constants.
No integration with other code‑gen workflows.
data.setup_notes: Add to pubspec, import package/ascii.dart or html_entity.dart, or run CLI to generate a file.
